title: Powers of i Repeat Every 4 Explained Simply | PUC Maths Class 11
description:
What is i to the power 103? It looks like a monster sum, but you can answer it in three seconds. Aarav wrote the powers of i in his notebook and saw the list repeat after four lines. In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Maths (NCERT Chapter 4, Complex Numbers and Quadratic Equations) we meet the imaginary unit i and find out why.

You will build the powers of i step by step from i squared = -1, watch a point make quarter turns on a live picture as the power n counts up, learn the divide-by-4 remainder shortcut (and why it works backwards for i to the -1), and see the difference between the two square roots of -1 and the symbol √-1. Two pause-and-think questions, a worked example where four powers in a row add to zero, the exam trap √-4 × √-9 ≠ 6, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

In this video:
0:00 What is i to the power 103?
0:29 The imaginary unit i
0:49 Building the powers of i
1:24 Live: each × i is a quarter turn
1:54 The divide-by-4 shortcut
2:41 Powers of i go round in fours
2:48 Square roots of negative numbers
3:29 Worked example: four powers in a row
4:12 Exam trap: √-4 × √-9
4:35 Where it is asked
4:44 Practice question (JEE Main pattern)
5:26 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode (Ep 39): Real and Imaginary Parts. Which street, which floor? Every complex number has two parts.
